title: Atoms and their parts
lede: Everything you can touch is made of atoms. Here's what's inside one.

sections.md:
## The three particles
| Particle | Charge | Where | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proton | + | nucleus | about 1 unit |
| Neutron | none | nucleus | about 1 unit |
| Electron | − | around the nucleus | about 1/1,836 of a proton |

The nucleus is tiny but holds almost all the mass. Electrons move in the space around it, and that space is most of the atom.

## What makes an element
The number of **protons** decides the element. Every carbon atom has 6 protons; every oxygen atom has 8. That number is the **atomic number**.

- Change the neutrons and you get an **isotope** of the same element (carbon-12 vs carbon-14).
- Change the electrons and you get an **ion**, an atom with a charge.

sections.problem: Sodium (Na) has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many protons, neutrons and electrons in a neutral atom?

sections.label: Why atoms bond
sections.md: Chemistry is mostly about electrons, especially the outermost ones. Atoms gain, lose or share electrons to reach a stable arrangement. That's what holds molecules together.
